questions.q: For the reversible reaction, N$_{2(g)}$ + 3H$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NH$_{3(g)}$. When the partial pressure is measured in atmosphere, the value of $K_p$ at 500$^\circ$C is $1.44 \times 10^{-5}$. The value of $K_c$ when the concentration is expressed in mol L$^{-1}$ is:
questions.explanation: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$ with $\Delta n = 2-4=-2$; using T = 773 K (500$^\circ$C) and R = 0.082, $K_c = K_p(RT)^{2} = \dfrac{1.44\times10^{-5}}{(0.082\times773)^{-2}}$.

questions.q: For the following gaseous reversible reaction: 3A$_{(g)}$ + B$_{(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ A$_3$B$_{(g)}$ ($\Delta H$ = -q kJ), the amount of product A$_3$B$_{(g)}$ is affected by
questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic (temperature affects the equilibrium position) and involves a decrease in gas moles (4 to 1), so pressure also shifts the equilibrium; a catalyst affects only the rate, not the equilibrium amount.

questions.q: A 0.15 mole of pyridinium chloride has been added to 500 cm$^3$ of 0.2M pyridine solution (a base). Assuming there is no change in volume upon mixing, the pH of the resulting solution is (Note: K$_b$ for pyridine is $1.5 \times 10^{-9}$)
questions.explanation: This pyridine/pyridinium buffer has moles base = 0.5 L $\times$ 0.2 M = 0.1 mol and moles salt = 0.15 mol; pOH = pK$_b$ + log(salt/base) = 8.82 + log(1.5) $\approx$ 9, so pH $\approx$ 5. KEA awarded grace marks for this question in the revised key.

questions.q: The group reagent NH$_4$Cl(s) and aqueous NH$_3$ will precipitate which of the following ion?
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl/NH$_3$ provides just enough OH$^-$ to exceed the low solubility product of Al(OH)$_3$, precipitating Al$^{3+}$ while Ca$^{2+}$ and Ba$^{2+}$ remain in solution.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true about equilibrium? (a) Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature (b) All the measurable properties of the system remain constant at equilibrium. (c) Equilibrium constant for the reverse reaction is the inverse of the equilibrium constant for the reaction in the forward direction.
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly describe features of chemical equilibrium: it requires a closed system at constant temperature, measurable properties stay constant, and K(reverse) = 1/K(forward).

questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, in the reaction CO(g) + 3H$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ CH$_4$(g) + H$_2$O(g), the formation of methane is favoured by (a) increasing the concentration of CO (b) increasing the concentration of H$_2$O (c) decreasing the concentration of CH$_4$ (d) decreasing the concentration of H$_2$
questions.explanation: Increasing a reactant (CO) or removing a product (CH$_4$) both shift the equilibrium forward, favouring methane formation, so (a) and (c) are correct.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant at 298K for the reaction A + B $\rightleftharpoons$ C + D is 100. If the initial concentrations of all the four species were 1M each, then equilibrium concentration of D (in mol L$^{-1}$) will be
questions.explanation: Letting x be the extent of reaction, $K_c = \dfrac{(1+x)^2}{(1-x)^2} = 100 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1+x}{1-x}=10 \Rightarrow x = 0.818$, so [D] = 1 + x = 1.818 M.

questions.q: In the analysis of III group basic radicals of salts, the purpose of adding NH$_4$Cl$_{(s)}$ to NH$_4$OH is:
options: to increase the concentration of OH$^-$ ions.
to precipitate the radicals of group IV and V.
to suppress the dissociation of NH$_4$OH.
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl provides NH$_4^+$ ions which, by the common ion effect, suppress the dissociation of NH$_4$OH so that only group III hydroxides are precipitated.

questions.q: Solubility product of CaC$_2$O$_4$ at a given temperature in pure water is $4\times10^{-9}$ (mol L$^{-1}$)$^2$. Solubility of CaC$_2$O$_4$ at the same temperature is

At 500 K, for a reversible reaction A$_{2(g)}$ + B$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2AB$_{(g)}$ in a closed container, K$_C$ = 2 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$. In the presence of catalyst, the equilibrium is attaining 10 times faster. The equilibrium constant K$_C$ in the presence of catalyst at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally by lowering the activation energy for both, so it does not change the equilibrium constant; K$_C$ remains 2 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$.

questions.q: A weak acid with pK$_a$ 5.9 and weak base with pK$_b$ 5.8 are mixed in equal proportions. pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: For a salt of a weak acid and a weak base, $pH = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2}(pK_a - pK_b) = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2}(5.9-5.8) = 7.05$.

questions.q: 1 mole of HI is heated in a closed container of capacity of 2 L. At equilibrium half a mole of HI is dissociated. The equilibrium constant of the reaction is
questions.explanation: 2HI $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$ + I$_2$: 0.5 mol HI dissociates, giving 0.25 mol each of H$_2$ and I$_2$ and leaving 0.5 mol HI. K$_c$ = [H$_2$][I$_2$]/[HI]$^2$ = (0.125 $\times$ 0.125)/(0.25)$^2$ = 0.25 (the volume cancels).

questions.q: Which among the following has highest pH?
questions.explanation: 1 M NaOH is the most concentrated strong base among the options, so it has the highest pH.

questions.q: For the reaction A(g) + B (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ C(g) + D(g); ΔH = − QKJ. The equilibrium constant cannot be disturbed by
questions.explanation: Since Δn$_{gas}$ = 0 for this reaction, changing pressure has no effect on the equilibrium constant (or even the equilibrium position); only temperature change alters K.

questions.q: K$_a$ values for acids H$_2$SO$_3$, HNO$_2$, CH$_3$COOH and HCN are respectively 1.3 × 10$^{-2}$, 4 ×10$^{-4}$, 1.8 × 10$^{-5}$ and 4 × 10$^{-10}$, which of the above acids produces stronger conjugate base in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: The weakest acid produces the strongest conjugate base. HCN has the smallest K$_a$, so it is the weakest acid and gives the strongest conjugate base (CN$^-$).

questions.q: The conjugate base of NH$_3$ is
questions.explanation: Removing a proton (H$^+$) from NH$_3$ gives the amide ion NH$_2^-$, its conjugate base.

questions.q: Solubility of AgCl is least in
questions.explanation: AlCl3 provides the highest concentration of common Cl- ion (0.3 M), so by the common-ion effect it suppresses the solubility of AgCl the most.

questions.q:
Match the following acids with their pKa values:
a. Phenol   i. 16
b. p-Nitrophenol   ii. 0.78
c. Ethanol   iii. 10
d. Picric acid   iv. 7.1
questions.explanation: Phenol (pKa$\approx$10), p-nitrophenol (pKa$\approx$7.1, more acidic due to -NO2), ethanol (pKa$\approx$16, weakly acidic), picric acid (pKa$\approx$0.78, strongly acidic) — matching a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: The relationship between K$_p$ and K$_c$ is K$_p$ = K$_c$(RT)$^{\Delta n}$. What would be the value of $\Delta n$ for the reaction NH$_4$Cl (s) $\rightleftharpoons$ NH$_3$ (g) + HCl (g) ?
questions.explanation: $\Delta n$ = moles of gaseous products $-$ moles of gaseous reactants = 2 $-$ 0 = 2.

questions.q: Acidity of BF$_3$ can be explained on which of the following concepts ?
options: Bronsted-Lowry as well as Lewis concept
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ has no OH or H$^+$ to donate; it accepts an electron pair (it is electron deficient), so its acidic behaviour is explained only by the Lewis concept.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant for the reaction N$_{2(g)}$ + O$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO$_{(g)}$ is $4\times10^{-4}$ at 2000 K. In presence of a catalyst the equilibrium is attained ten times faster. Therefore the equilibrium constant in presence of catalyst at 2000 K is
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up attainment of equilibrium but does not change the equilibrium constant, so K$_c$ stays $4\times10^{-4}$.

questions.q: The reaction quotient 'Q$_c$' is useful in predicting the direction of the reaction. Which of the following is incorrect ?
options: If Q$_c$ > K$_c$, the reverse reaction is favoured
If Q$_c$ < K$_c$, the forward reaction is favoured
If Q$_c$ = K$_c$, no reaction occurs
If Q$_c$ > K$_c$, forward reaction is favoured
questions.explanation: When Q$_c$ > K$_c$ the system shifts in the reverse direction, not forward, to reach equilibrium, so statement D is incorrect.

questions.q: In the reaction; Fe(OH)$_3$(s) $\rightleftharpoons$ Fe$^{3+}$(aq) + 3OH$^-$(aq), if the concentration of OH$^-$ ions is decreased by $\dfrac{1}{4}$ times, then the equilibrium concentration of Fe$^{3+}$ will increase by,
questions.explanation: K$_{sp}$ = [Fe$^{3+}$][OH$^-$]$^3$ is constant; if [OH$^-$] becomes 1/4, [Fe$^{3+}$] must increase by $4^3$ = 64 times to keep K$_{sp}$ constant.

questions.q: Equilibrium constants K$_1$ and K$_2$ for the following equilibria (a) NO(g) + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ NO$_2$(g) (b) 2NO$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO(g) + O$_2$(g) are related as :
questions.explanation: Reaction (b) is the reverse of 2 $\times$ reaction (a); doubling (a) squares K$_1$, and reversing inverts it, giving $K_2 = 1/K_1^2$.

questions.q: The aqueous solution of following salt will have the lowest pH:
questions.explanation: HClO$_4$ is the strongest acid among HClO, HClO$_2$, HClO$_3$ and HClO$_4$, so its conjugate base ClO$_4^-$ hydrolyses the least; a NaClO$_4$ solution stays closest to neutral (lowest pH among these basic salt solutions).

questions.q: The pair of compound which cannot exist together in solution is
questions.explanation: NaHCO$_3$ and NaOH react together (NaHCO$_3$ + NaOH $\rightarrow$ Na$_2$CO$_3$ + H$_2$O), so they cannot coexist in solution.

questions.q: In presence of HCl, H$_2$S results the precipitation of Group-2 elements but not Gp-4 elements during qualitative analysis. It is due to
questions.explanation: HCl provides a common H$^+$ ion that suppresses the ionisation of the weak acid H$_2$S (common-ion effect), lowering the S$^{2-}$ concentration enough to exceed only the low K$_{sp}$ of Group-2 sulphides, not the more soluble Group-4 sulphides.

questions.q:
One mole of ammonia was completely absorbed in one litre solution each of (a) 1M HCl, (b) 1M CH$_3$COOH and (c) 1M H$_2$SO$_4$ at 298 K.

The decreasing order for the pH of the resulting solutions is

(Given K$_b$(NH$_3$) = 4.74)
questions.explanation: With HCl, all NH$_3$ is neutralised to NH$_4$Cl (acidic salt, low pH); with CH$_3$COOH, NH$_4$CH$_3$COO forms (nearly neutral, higher pH); with H$_2$SO$_4$ (only 0.5 mol needed to neutralise), excess NH$_3$ remains, making it most basic — so c > b > a. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q:
For the equilibrium: CaCO$_{3(s)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ CaO$_{(s)}$ + CO$_{2(g)}$; K$_p$ = 1.64 atm at 1000 K

50 g of CaCO$_3$ in a 10 litre closed vessel is heated to 1000 K. Percentage of CaCO$_3$ that remains unreacted at equilibrium is

(Given R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: K$_p$ = P(CO$_2$) = 1.64 atm; moles CO$_2$ at equilibrium = PV/RT = 1.64×10/(0.082×1000) = 0.2 mol = moles CaCO$_3$ decomposed (20 g); initial moles CaCO$_3$ = 50/100 = 0.5 mol, so 0.2 mol reacted means 0.3 mol (60%) remains unreacted.

questions.q: The yield of the products in the reaction, A$_{2(g)}$ + 2B$_{(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ C$_{(g)}$ + Q. kJ would be higher at
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic and decreases moles of gas (3 mol to 1 mol), so low temperature and high pressure favour higher yield by Le Chatelier's principle.

questions.q: An example for a neutral buffer is
questions.explanation: A mixture of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a weak base (ammonium hydroxide) of comparable strength gives a nearly neutral buffer.

questions.q: Conjugate base of H$_2$PO$_4^-$ is
questions.explanation: Removing one H$^+$ from H$_2$PO$_4^-$ gives its conjugate base HPO$_4^{2-}$.

questions.q: Identify a species which is 'NOT' a Bronsted acid but a Lewis acid.
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ has no proton to donate (not a Bronsted acid) but accepts an electron pair, making it a Lewis acid.

questions.q: The pH of 10$^{-8}$M HCl solution is
questions.explanation: At such low concentration, contribution of water's autoionization must be included: [H$^+$] $\approx$ 1.05$\times$10$^{-7}$ M, giving pH $\approx$ 6.9586, slightly less than 7.

questions.q: The pH of the solution obtained by mixing 100 ml of a solution of pH = 3 with 400 ml of a solution of pH = 4 is
questions.explanation: Total moles H$^+$ $=100\times10^{-3}\times10^{-3}+400\times10^{-3}\times10^{-4}=1.4\times10^{-4}$ mol in 0.5 L, so $[H^+]=2.8\times10^{-4}$ M, giving pH $=4-\log2.8$.

questions.q: 5 ml of 0.4 N NaOH is mixed with 20 ml of 0.1 N HCl. The pH of the resulting solution will be
questions.explanation: Milliequivalents of NaOH $=5\times0.4=2$; of HCl $=20\times0.1=2$; they exactly neutralize each other giving a neutral solution, pH = 7.

questions.q: On adding which of the following, the pH of 20 ml of 0.1 N HCl will not alter?
questions.explanation: 0.1 N HCl has pH = 1; adding 500 ml of HCl of the same pH (=1, i.e. same [H$^+$]) does not change the pH of the solution.

questions.q: 2 moles of N$_2$O$_4$(g) is kept in a closed container at 298 K and under 1 atm pressure. It is heated to 596 K when 20% by mass of N$_2$O$_4$(g) decomposes to NO$_2$. The resulting pressure is
questions.explanation: N$_2$O$_4\rightleftharpoons2NO_2$; 20% of 2 mol = 0.4 mol dissociates, giving 1.6 mol N$_2$O$_4$ left + 0.8 mol NO$_2$ = 2.4 mol total (n$_1$=2 initially). Using $\dfrac{P_1V}{n_1T_1}=\dfrac{P_2V}{n_2T_2}$: $P_2=1\times\dfrac{2.4}{2}\times\dfrac{596}{298}=2.4$ atm.

questions.q:
Consider the following gaseous equilibria with equilibrium constants $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively.
$SO_{2(g)}+\dfrac{1}{2}O_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons SO_{3(g)}$
$2SO_{3(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2SO_{2(g)}+O_{2(g)}$
The equilibrium constants are related as ..............
questions.explanation: The second equation is the reverse of the first, doubled, so $K_2=(1/K_1)^2=1/K_1^2$, i.e. $K_1^2=1/K_2$.

questions.q: For the reversible reaction, $A_{(s)}+B_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons C_{(g)}+D_{(g)}$, $\Delta G^0=-350\\ kJ$, which one of the following statements is true?
options: Equilibrium constant is greater than one.
questions.explanation: A large negative $\Delta G^0$ gives $K=e^{-\Delta G^0/RT}\gg1$, so the equilibrium constant is much greater than one.

questions.q: pH value of which one of the following is NOT equal to one?
questions.explanation: $CH_3COOH$ is a weak acid and is not fully dissociated, so its pH is greater than 1; the other three all give $[H^+]=0.1$ M, i.e. pH=1.

questions.q: A buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of sodium acetate dissolved in 1000 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M acetic acid. To the above buffer solution, 0.1 mole of sodium acetate is further added and dissolved. The pH of the resulting buffer is ..............
questions.explanation: Initially moles acetate = moles acid = 0.1 (pH=$pK_a$); after adding 0.1 more mole of acetate, [salt]/[acid]=0.2/0.1=2, so pH=$pK_a+\log2$ by the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

questions.q: $H_2S$ is passed into one dm$^3$ of a solution containing 0.1 mole of $Zn^{2+}$ and 0.01 mole of $Cu^{2+}$ till the sulphide ion concentration reaches $8.1\times10^{-19}$ moles. Which one of the following statements is true? [$K_{sp}$ of $ZnS$ and $CuS$ are $3\times10^{-22}$ and $8\times10^{-36}$ respectively]
questions.explanation: $Q_{ZnS}=0.1\times8.1\times10^{-19}=8.1\times10^{-20}>K_{sp}(ZnS)$ and $Q_{CuS}=0.01\times8.1\times10^{-19}=8.1\times10^{-21}\gg K_{sp}(CuS)$, so both salts exceed their $K_{sp}$ and precipitate.

questions.q: 0.023 g of sodium metal is reacted with 100 cm$^3$ of water. The pH of the resulting solution is ..............

Consider the following gaseous equilibria with equilibrium constants $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively.

$SO_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}O_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons SO_{3(g)}$

$2SO_{3(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2SO_{2(g)} + O_{2(g)}$

The equilibrium constants are related as .......................
questions.explanation: Reaction 2 is the reverse of reaction 1, doubled: $K_2 = (1/K_1)^2$, so $K_1^2 = 1/K_2$.

questions.q:
For the reversible reaction

$A_{(s)} + B_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons C_{(g)} + D_{(g)}$ : $\Delta G^0 = -350\ kJ$.

Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Equilibrium constant is greater than one.
The reaction is thermodynamically not feasible.
questions.explanation: Since $\Delta G^0 = -RT\ln K$ is large and negative, $K \gg 1$, i.e. the equilibrium constant is greater than one.

questions.q: 0.023 g of sodium metal is reacted with 100 cm$^3$ of water. The pH of the resulting solution is ...................
questions.explanation: Moles Na = 0.023/23 = 0.001 giving 0.001 mol NaOH in 0.1 L, so [OH$^-$] = 0.01 M, pOH = 2, pH = 12.

questions.q: A buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of sodium acetate dissolved in 1000 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M acetic acid. To the above buffer solution, 0.1 mole of sodium acetate is further added and dissolved. The pH of the resulting buffer is equal to ...............
questions.explanation: After addition, salt = 0.2 mol, acid = 0.1 mol; $pH = pK_a + \log(0.2/0.1) = pK_a + \log 2$.

questions.q:
One dm$^3$ solution containing $10^{-5}$ moles each of $Cl^-$ ions and $CrO_4^{-2}$ ions is treated with $10^{-4}$ mole of silver nitrate. Which one of the following observations is made?

$[K_{SP}\ Ag_2CrO_4 = 4\times10^{-12}]$

$[K_{SP}\ AgCl = 1\times10^{-10}]$
options: Both silver chromate and silver chloride start precipitating simultaneously.
questions.explanation: AgCl requires a much lower [Ag$^+$] to reach its $K_{sp}$ (10$^{-10}$/10$^{-5}$ = 10$^{-5}$ M) than Ag$_2$CrO$_4$ (needs $\sqrt{4\times10^{-12}/10^{-5}} \approx 2\times10^{-4}$ M), so AgCl precipitates first as Ag$^+$ is added.

questions.q: pH value of which one of the following is not equal to one?
options: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.4 M $HCl$ + 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$
questions.explanation: 0.1 M CH$_3$COOH is a weak acid, only partially ionized, so its pH is greater than 1, unlike the other three which all give [H$^+$] = 0.1 M (pH = 1).

questions.q: 5 moles of SO$_2$ and 5 moles of O$_2$ are allowed to react. At equilibrium, it was found that 60% of SO$_2$ is used up. If the partial pressure of the equilibrium mixture is one atmosphere, the partial pressure of O$_2$ is
questions.explanation: 3 mol SO$_2$ reacts, consuming 1.5 mol O$_2$; remaining moles: SO$_2$=2, O$_2$=3.5, SO$_3$=3, total=8.5. $p_{O_2} = (3.5/8.5)\times1 \approx 0.41$ atm.

questions.q: 2HI(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$(g) + I$_2$(g). The equilibrium constant of the above reaction is 6.4 at 300 K. If 0.25 mole each of H$_2$ and I$_2$ are added to the system, the equilibrium constant will be
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant depends only on temperature, so it remains 6.4 regardless of the amounts added.

questions.q: 30 cc of $\dfrac{M}{3}$ HCl, 20 cc of $\dfrac{M}{2}$ HNO$_3$ and 40 cc of $\dfrac{M}{4}$ NaOH solutions are mixed and the volume was made up to 1 dm$^3$. The pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Moles: HCl=0.01, HNO$_3$=0.01 (total acid 0.02), NaOH=0.01; excess acid = 0.01 mol in 1 L gives [H$^+$]=0.01 M, so pH = 2.

questions.q: $10^{-6}$ M NaOH is diluted 100 times. The pH of the diluted base is
questions.explanation: Diluting to $10^{-8}$ M NaOH, the contribution from water's autoionisation dominates, giving a pH just above 7, i.e. between 7 and 8.
